title: [dynamo] Meta-issue: torch.compile gaps found via the CPython test suite
body:
I asked an agent to look at the graph break messages from the CPython test suite and
summarize the missing features in Dynamo. This is not an exhaustive list of all missing
features, but it contains some of the gaps that we want to close in the near term.

Some items are harder than they look (`functools.lru_cache` is the usual example).

## How to run

```bash
# one module
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1 python test/cpython/v3_13/test_iter.py -v

# one test
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1 python test/cpython/v3_13/test_iter.py -v -k test_countOf
```

PyTorch must be built against Python 3.13. A known-failing test reports as `skipped` with
the graph-break reason attached, because it has a file under
`test/dynamo_expected_failures/CPython313-<module>-<Class>.<test>`. **Deleting that file is
part of your fix** - CI fails the test as an unexpected success otherwise.

---

## Shared root causes

The six items below each account for several failures across unrelated modules. Fixing one
unlocks every test listed under it, which makes these the highest-leverage work in this
issue.

### 1. `type.__new__` on a C-implemented type

`Unsupported method call: type.__new__`. This is the general "constructing any
non-allowlisted C-implemented type" gap, confirmed at four unrelated call sites. Probably
the single highest-leverage fix here.

- [ ] `test_functools.py::TestLRUPy::test_lru_no_args` and `TestLRUC::test_lru_no_args` - `@lru_cache` decoration
- [x] `test_set.py::TestSetSubclass::test_keywords_in_subclass` - `set`/`frozenset` subclassing (#196425)
- [ ] `test_sys.py::ExceptHookTest::test_excepthook` - `io.StringIO()` construction
- [ ] `test_contextlib.py::TestRedirectStdout::test_enter_result_is_target` - `io.StringIO()` construction

### 2. `Read uninitialized cell` (gb0091)

One root cause, eight tests, four unrelated modules - containers, exceptions, iterators.

- [ ] `test_list.py::ListTest::test_repr_mutate`
- [ ] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_getitem`
- [ ] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_reentrant_insertion`
- [ ] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_str_nonstr`
- [ ] `test_set.py::_TestJointOps::test_deepcopy`
- [ ] `test_exceptions.py::NameErrorTests::test_gh_111654`
- [ ] `test_iter.py::TestCase::test_3720`
- [ ] `test_iter.py::TestCase::test_free_after_iterating`

### 3. Detected user errors don't surface as the real exception

Dynamo already knows the call is invalid, but instead of raising the `TypeError` CPython
would raise, it produces a generic wrapper, an internal crash, or an
`InternalTorchDynamoError`. Three severities, same underlying gap: user errors detected
during tracing need a path to "raise the real exception."

Generic `Unsupported: invalid call to builtin op handler` instead of a real `TypeError`
(`variables/builtin.py`, builtin-call argument binding):

- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_filter` (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_isinstance` (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_issubclass` (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_map` (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::TestSorted::test_bad_arguments` (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::TestSorted::test_baddecorator` (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::TestType::test_bad_args` (#196432)
- [x] `except 42:` - graph-breaks with `Exception with bad expected type`, CPython raises `TypeError` (#196432)
- [x] `except (ValueError, 42):` - tuple with a bad member (#196432)
- [x] `except <instance>:` - an instance, not a class (#196432)
- [x] `except "string":` (#196432)

Dynamo's own argument validation crashes:

- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_hasattr` - `hasattr(sys, 1)` crashes Dynamo's arg validation (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_setattr` - `setattr(sys, 1, 'spam')`, same shape (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_getattr` - zero-arg `getattr()` gives a bare `IndexError` from Dynamo's arg-binding code (#196526)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::BuiltinTest::test_hash` - `hash()` on a custom object: `AssertionError: Cannot construct ConstantVariable` (#196432)
- [x] `test_builtin.py::TestType::test_type_doc` - `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'debug_repr'`, a bug in Dynamo's own debug formatting (#197145, #198153)
- [x] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_invalid_keyword_arguments` - kwarg-binding `TypeError` crashes Dynamo (#196432)

Real error leaks as `InternalTorchDynamoError` instead of a clean graph break:

- [x] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test_bad_first_arg` - `TypeError` for invalid `super()` args (#196432, #196061)
- [x] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test_supercheck_fail` - same leak (#196432, #196061)
- [x] `test_descr.py::ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_slot_shadows_class_variable` - `ValueError: 'foo' in __slots__ conflicts with class variable` (#196432)
- [x] `test_descr.py::ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_slots_special2` - `TypeError: __classcell__ must be a nonlocal cell` (#196432)

### 4. Missing `python_type()` on attribute chains

Attribute access on an object Dynamo models only partially produces a `GetAttrVariable`
chain with no `python_type()`. Same failure text, three unrelated object kinds.

- [ ] Tracebacks (PEP 626): `tb_frame.f_lineno` gives `GetAttrVariable(GetAttrVariable(TracebackVariable(), tb_frame), f_lineno) does not implement python_type()`. Confirmed on 6 sampled `test_exceptions.py::PEP626Tests` methods; 10 share the identical shape, so one fix likely closes all 10.
- [x] `test_generators.py::GeneratorTest::test_name` - `gen.__name__` has no type (#196887)
- [ ] `test_generators.py::GeneratorTest::test_gi_frame_f_back`
- [ ] `test_generators.py::ModifyUnderlyingIterableTest::test_modify_f_locals` - `gi_frame.f_locals`
- [ ] `test_generators.py::YieldFromTests::test_generator_gi_yieldfrom` - `gi_running`
- [ ] `test_generators.py::GeneratorTest::test_cr_frame_f_back` - `cr_frame` isn't modeled on coroutines at all (`AttributeError('cr_frame')`)
- [ ] `warnings.catch_warnings()` / `assertWarns` - `CatchWarningsCtxManagerVariable` is missing `python_type()`

### 5. Skip detection: "cannot determine source file"

`Attempted to call function marked as skipped`. `cmath` was an all-or-nothing module gap
here - 26 of 29 `test_cmath.py` failures were this one cause. `math` gets per-function
dispatch and `cmath` did not.

- [x] all `cmath.*` functions (#195999)
- [ ] `test_math.py::MathTests::testSumProd`
- [ ] `test_math.py::MathTests::test_sumprod_accuracy`
- [ ] `test_math.py::MathTests::test_sumprod_extended_precision_accuracy`
- [ ] `test_math.py::MathTests::test_sumprod_stress`

### 6. `copy` / `deepcopy` / `pickle` are unmodeled

No trace rule or polyfill exists for any of these; they surface wherever a type implements
the protocols. See the Copy / deepcopy / pickle section below.

---

## Correctness bugs

Compiles, no exception, no graph break, wrong answer. Prioritize over everything below
regardless of how narrow the trigger looks.

- [ ] Enum's metaclass makes a property/method-shadowing member break guard construction (`AttributeError: 'fget'`) - sometimes silently computes a wrong value instead of erroring
- [ ] Enum member write/delete protection not enforced - mutation silently allowed where CPython raises `AttributeError`

`__class__` cell resolves to `None` or a wrong value in `super()`-adjacent constructions.
Same feature area as the already-fixed `__build_class__` closure-cell work; these shapes
still regress:

- [ ] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test___class___delayed`
- [ ] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test___class___mro`
- [ ] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test___class___new`
- [ ] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test_various___class___pathologies`

Malformed `__classcell__` / `super()` argument patterns don't raise where CPython does -
Dynamo is too permissive:

- [ ] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test___classcell___missing`
- [ ] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test___classcell___overwrite`
- [ ] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test___classcell___wrong_cell`
- [x] `test_super.py::TestSuper::test_super_argtype` (#196061)

## Copy / deepcopy / pickle

- [ ] `copy.deepcopy()` unsupported outright - no trace rule or polyfill at all (hits Enum, OrderedDict, and more)
- [ ] `pickle.dumps()` unsupported across every type tested, no exceptions
- [ ] `list.copy()` - the method, not the free function; skipped builtin
- [ ] `dict.copy()` - same
- [ ] `set.copy()` - same
- [ ] `OrderedDict()` construction - `Unexpected type in sourceless builder`
- [ ] `test_deque.py::TestBasic::test_deepcopy` - `deque` + `copy.deepcopy`, unsupported method call

## Object model / metaclasses

- [x] `type.mro()` called as a method - unsupported (#196863, user-defined classes only)
- [ ] Metaclass-driven class creation (`__call__`, `__prepare__` overrides) - unsupported
- [ ] Dynamic class creation via `type()` with a custom metaclass - unsupported
- [ ] `super().__new__()` - deliberately rejected by Dynamo, hit heavily by Enum's `__new__` chains
- [x] `test_builtin.py::TestType::test_type_typeparams` - `CALL_INTRINSIC_1` for PEP 695 `type X[T] = ...`. There is a handler for *some* intrinsics but not this one, so treat the opcode as partially supported rather than done. (#198203)
- [x] `DELETE_GLOBAL` - `del` on a module global (#197056)

## Descriptors: property

Property `AttributeError` messages: the attribute name is now included, but the class name
is wrong (bare `'cls'` instead of CPython's fully-qualified `'Outer.cls'`):

- [x] `test_property.py::_PropertyUnreachableAttribute::{test_del_property,test_set_property}`, both `WithName` and `NoName` variants (#196080)

`property()` builtin-call argument-shape gaps - one root cause, narrow argument-binding
coverage:

- [x] full positional form (`property(get, None, None, "doc")`) (#197378)
- [x] kwargs-only form (#197378)
- [x] non-function `fget` (#197378)
- [x] single-positional form (#197378)

Subclassing `property` itself - unsupported:

- [ ] `test_property.py::PropertySubclassTests::test_issue41287`
- [ ] `test_property.py::PropertySubclassTests::test_property_with_slots_no_docstring`
- [ ] `test_property.py::PropertySubclassTests::test_property_with_slots_docstring_silently_dropped`
- [ ] `test_property.py::PropertySubclassTests::test_property_with_slots_and_doc_slot_docstring_present`

Dynamo-internal crashes:

- [ ] `test_property.py::PropertySubclassTests::test_slots_docstring_copy_exception` - `AttributeError: '__doc__' is read-only`
- [ ] `test_property.py::PropertyTests::test_property___isabstractmethod__descriptor` - empty-message `ValueError`

## Descriptors: super()

Construction and attribute-resolution cluster in `SuperVariable` (`variables/misc.py`).
All in `test_super.py::TestSuper` unless noted.

- [x] `test_cell_as_self` (#196061, #196432)
- [ ] `test_obscure_super_errors`
- [x] `test_super___class__` (#196061)
- [x] `test_super_argcount` (#196061)
- [x] `test_attribute_error` - `"Unable to resolve super getattr"` (#196061)
- [ ] `test_reassigned_new`
- [ ] `test_shadowed_dynamic`
- [ ] `test_shadowed_dynamic_two_arg`
- [ ] `test_unusual_getattro`
- [x] `test_super_in_class_methods_working` - internal invariant `AssertionError: source must not be None for classmethod resolution` fires as a bare test failure on legitimate user code (#196061)
- [ ] `test_super_init_leaks` - `super().__init__` dispatch to an unmodeled type (`missing tp_init`)
- [ ] `super()` attribute resolution gives up for certain resolved-attribute shapes

(`test_bad_first_arg` and `test_supercheck_fail` are in shared root cause #3.)

## Descriptors: test_descr.py

- [x] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_special_unbound_method_types` - `list.__add__ == list.__add__` hits `Missing tp_richcompare_impl override` on `WrapperDescriptorVariable`. Before the recent change, `list.__add__` wasn't resolved as a real descriptor at all (generic `GetAttrVariable`); now that it resolves correctly, comparing two of them has no equality support. Contained follow-up in `variables/functions.py`. (#197788)

`setattr()` unsupported - first found on `type`/`property`, confirmed to generalize to plain
user-defined classes:

- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_properties`
- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_dynamics`
- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_set_doc`
- [ ] `test_iter.py::TestCase::test_ref_counting_behavior` - plain `setattr(SomeClass, 'attr', val)`

Calling the `classmethod`/`staticmethod` builtin directly rather than as a decorator:

- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_classmethods` - real gap
- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_classmethods_in_c` - low value, CPython test-fixture specific
- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_staticmethods` - low value
- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_staticmethods_in_c` - low value
- [x] `classmethod(fn)` called as a plain builtin - unsupported (#197781)

- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_meth_class_get` - `classmethod_descriptor` has no `tp_descr_get_impl`; adjacent to the recent `tp_descr_get_impl` work but this descriptor type isn't covered
- [ ] `OperatorsTest::test_explicit_reverse_methods` - `__radd__`/reverse-operator dispatch via `type`
- [x] `DictProxyTests::test_repr` - `mappingproxy` missing `tp_repr_impl` (#196902)
- [ ] `ClassPropertiesAndMethods::test_compattr` - `Unexpected type in sourceless builder` on a computed-attribute descriptor class

## Exception handling

- [ ] `test_exceptions.py::ExceptionTests::testChainingAttrs` - **constructing a custom exception subclass is unsupported.** A locally-defined `class MyException(BaseException): pass` with no custom `__new__` fails: `Unsupported user-defined object construction during side-effect tracking ... BaseException.__new__(MyException) is not safe`. Very common real-world pattern.
- [ ] `test_exceptions.py::ExceptionTests::testKeywordArgs` - keyword args to exception constructors (`BaseException(a=1)`)
- [x] `test_exceptions.py::ExceptionTests::test_notes` - `BaseException.add_note()` (PEP 678), a commonly-used modern API (#197415)
- [x] `test_exceptions.py::ExceptionTests::test_invalid_delattr` - `__delattr__` on exception instances (#196722)
- [x] `test_raise.py::TestRaise::test_assert_with_tuple_arg` - `assert x, <non-string message>`; CPython allows any object as the assert message (#197798)

`except X as e:` cleanup-name semantics - CPython auto-`del`s `e` at block exit, so reading
it afterwards is a legitimate `NameError`; Dynamo raises `Unsupported: Attempted to read
undefined local variable`. Distinct from the generic `assertRaises` harness limitation -
this is a specific language-level guarantee:

- [ ] `test_exceptions.py::ExceptionTests::test_exception_cleanup_names`
- [ ] `test_exceptions.py::ExceptionTests::test_exception_cleanup_names2`

- [ ] Exceptions escaping the top-level compiled frame (`assertRaises`-shaped tests) - a general harness/tracing limitation, not one missing feature

## Containers

Self-referential container `repr()` guard (the `[...]` / `{...}` placeholder) doesn't work:

- [ ] `test_set.py::_TestJointOps::test_cyclical_repr`
- [ ] `test_userlist.py::UserListTest::test_repr`
- [ ] `test_userdict.py::UserDictTest::test_repr`

- [ ] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_fromkeys` - `dict.fromkeys()` on a dict subclass doesn't return an instance of that subclass; classmethod-dispatch gap
- [ ] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_items_symmetric_difference` - **Dynamo generates syntactically invalid Python**: an `IndentationError` in the generated code. A real codegen bug. (#196891 fixes the diagnostic crash; the test still graph-breaks on a data-dependent branch)
- [x] `test_range.py::RangeTest::test_index` - crashes on a custom-`__eq__` object hitting a constant-folding assumption (#196711)
- [ ] `list_tests.py::CommonTest::test_repr_deep` - deeply-nested `repr()` blows Dynamo's own trace recursion into a `RecursionError`
- [ ] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_copy_fuzz` - see Unconfirmed

## Generators / iterators

Generator and coroutine introspection is in shared root cause #4. Remaining:

- [ ] `test_iter.py::TestCase::test_exception_locations` - not a graph break but an `AssertionError`: traceback location metadata (`f_lasti`, column positions) doesn't match eager after Dynamo's bytecode rewriting. Real but narrow introspection-fidelity divergence, not a computation-correctness bug.

## Builtins / cells / function attributes

Cell objects - construction, mutation, `repr`, and rich comparison. The last is the same
family as the `WrapperDescriptorVariable` richcmp gap in `test_descr.py`.

- [ ] `test_funcattrs.py::FunctionPropertiesTest::test_cell_new` - construction unsupported
- [ ] `test_funcattrs.py::FunctionPropertiesTest::test_set_cell` - mutation unsupported
- [ ] `test_funcattrs.py::FunctionPropertiesTest::test___closure__` - `tp_repr_impl not implemented`
- [x] `test_funcattrs.py::CellTest::test_comparison` - missing `tp_richcompare_impl` (#197189)

- [ ] `test_funcattrs.py::FunctionPropertiesTest::test___globals__` - untraced builtin operator call path
- [x] `test_funcattrs.py::StaticMethodAttrsTest::test_func_attribute` - same (#197781)
- [ ] `test_funcattrs.py::FunctionPropertiesTest::test_invalid___code___assignment` - `Unsupported python_type() call`
- [ ] `test_funcattrs.py::InstancemethodAttrTest::test___func___non_method` - `Unsupported function call`
- [x] `contextlib.closing` - unsupported (confirmed independently in `test_contextlib.py`) (#197830)
- [x] `bytes()` with zero arguments - unsupported (narrow) (#196103)
- [x] `operator.length_hint()` - doesn't replicate CPython's `NotImplemented`-fallback behavior (#196901)
- [ ] Tensor `<` comparison inside a generic comparison test - possibly a real tensor-ops gap, not environmental

## math / cmath

No silently-wrong results in this area; every failure is a clean graph break or a
deliberate skip. Skip-detection items are in shared root cause #5.

Math builtins with custom-object arguments (`__index__`/`__ceil__`/`__floor__`/`__trunc__`)
aren't converted to a proxy - `Missing as_proxy() implementation`. All
`test_math.py::MathTests`:

- [x] `testGcd` (#197222)
- [x] `test_lcm` (#197222)
- [x] `testCeil` (#196867)
- [x] `testFloor` (#196867)
- [x] `test_trunc` (#196867)
- [x] `test_issue39871` (#197498)
- [ ] `test_prod`

`decimal.Decimal` / `fractions.Fraction` aren't modeled as tracked types at all, so they
fail as math/cmath arguments:

- [ ] `test_math.py::MathTests::testFactorialNonIntegers`
- [ ] `test_math.py::MathTests::testHypotAccuracy`
- [ ] `test_math.py::IsCloseTests::test_decimals`
- [ ] `test_math.py::IsCloseTests::test_fractions`


## Unconfirmed

Reproduced once but not stable, or not yet explained. **Re-verify on current HEAD before
starting.**

- [ ] `set.copy()` returned a wrong (empty) result silently. A later re-check reproduced it as a clean graph break instead (`Unsupported: id() comparison`) - possibly a different code path, or state drifted across an in-flight `copy`/`reduce_ex` fix.
- [ ] `test_dict.py::DictTest::test_copy_fuzz` unexpectedly hits `Tensor.item()`. Flagged by two independent survey passes, still unexplained.
- [ ] `test_math.py::MathTests::testDist` - `math.dist()` hits a data-dependent-output op (`aten._local_scalar_dense.default`). Unclear why a Tensor op is involved in a plain-float distance calculation.

title: [inductor] With freezing on CPU, x.copy_(self.conv(x)) leaves x unchanged
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

```python
import torch


class M(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv = torch.nn.Conv2d(4, 4, 3, padding=1, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x):
        x.copy_(self.conv(x))
        return x


torch.manual_seed(0)
m = M().eval()
x = torch.rand(4, 4, 6, 6)
with torch.no_grad(), torch._inductor.config.patch(freezing=True):
    x_eager, x_comp = x.clone(), x.clone()
    m(x_eager)
    torch.compile(m)(x_comp)
print((x_eager - x_comp).abs().max().item(), (x_comp - x).abs().max().item())
```

```
1.6600873470306396 0.0
```

The compiled module doesn't update `x` at all, and returns it. `x[1:] = self.conv(x)[:-1]` does the same. Right without freezing, and on CUDA with freezing. 2.9.1, 2.14.0 and the 21 Sep nightly.

The post-grad graph is `_convolution_pointwise(arg1_1, ...)` then `copy_(arg1_1, ...)`; the output code copies `arg1_1` into a channels-last `buf0`, runs the convolution on it, and then writes the result into a buffer that reuses `buf0`, never into `arg1_1`. I think it's this block of `GraphLowering.run_node`: when a node has several users and one of them is an mkldnn convolution taking it as input, the node is rebound to `require_stride_order(result, channels_last)`. For a graph input, which has a fixed layout, that's a copy, and every other user, the `copy_` included, then gets the copy instead of the input. Skipping the rebinding for placeholders (the convolution's own lowering makes the copy it needs) makes both cases right. I have it with a test and can open a PR.

title: Context parallel does not cover sequential Gated DeltaNet layers
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`context_parallel()` does not support Gated DeltaNet.

It only intercepts SDPA and FlexAttention. Hybrid models such as Qwen3.5 mix those full-attention layers with GDN. GDN is a recurrence along time, so the Ring-style KV rotation used for SDPA cannot run it. GDN layers therefore cannot enter the same `context_parallel()` context, and sequence-sharded training of this architecture is blocked.

### Alternatives

Shard only the SDPA layers and leave GDN unsharded. GDN activations then stay full-sequence on every rank, which will have lower efficiency in memory and time.

### Additional context

Follow-up of #197487, now targeting `main`.

title: [MPS] linalg solves return row-major where CPU and CUDA return column-major
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`linalg.solve_triangular`, `cholesky_solve` and `linalg.solve` return a row-major result on MPS where CPU and CUDA return column-major. (makes for a runtime error -> see below)

```python
import torch

torch.manual_seed(0)
a = torch.randn(5, 5)
a = a @ a.T + 5 * torch.eye(5)
L = torch.linalg.cholesky(a)
B = torch.randn(5, 5)

for dev in ("cpu", "mps"):
    print(dev, torch.linalg.solve_triangular(L.to(dev), B.to(dev), upper=False).stride())
```

```text
cpu (1, 5)
mps (5, 1)
```

`cholesky_solve` and `linalg.solve` do the same. Values agree to ~6e-08.

Eager returns whatever the kernel produced and nothing checks that layout against a prediction, so this stays invisible in the eager suites. The compile path does catch it, but `instantiate_device_type_tests(TestInductorOpInfo, ...)` in `test/inductor/test_torchinductor_opinfo.py` doesn't produce an MPS class, so none of these ops are compiled on MPS in CI. Under `torch.compile` inductor bakes the meta's predicted stride into the generated code and it fails at runtime:

```text
AssertionError: expected size 5==5, stride 5==1 at dim=0; expected size 5==5, stride 1==5 at dim=1
Error in op: torch.ops.aten.linalg_solve_triangular.default
```

Eager users doing `.view()` or `.reshape()` on the result, or passing it to anything stride-sensitive, already get device-dependent behaviour today.

There are three layers to it:

1. The kernel ignores the output's strides. `linalg_solve_triangular_mps_impl` in `aten/src/ATen/native/mps/operations/LinearAlgebra.mm` calls `resize_output(out, ...)` then writes raw bytes through `getMTLBufferStorage(out)` with an `MPSMatrixDescriptor` whose `rowBytes` is `cols * elemSize`. That path is row-major only. It also means a caller-supplied non-row-contiguous `out` silently receives transposed data.

2. The C++ meta already carves MPS out. `TORCH_META_FUNC(_linalg_solve_ex)` in `aten/src/ATen/native/BatchLinearAlgebra.cpp:604`:

```cpp
auto result_strides = at::native::batched_matrix_contiguous_strides(
    result_shape, /*f_contig=*/A.device().type() != at::kMPS ? left : false);
```

with the same pattern for `LU_strides` on line 612. The Python meta `_linalg_solve_ex` in `torch/_meta_registrations.py:1901` is unconditionally F-contiguous. The two disagree and inductor uses the Python one.

3. The contract doesn't look like it's meant to be device-dependent. The Python metas, the C++ metas for the other linalg ops (`cholesky_ex`, `lu_factor_ex`, `lu_solve`, `inv_ex`) and eager probes of `cholesky` and `lu_solve` all agree on F-contiguous.

Reproduces with stock `torch==2.14.0` and a source build of `2.15.0a0+gitc5a3ee1` (main at c5a3ee18b93).

title: [inductor] y.index_put_((mask,), v) with a mask that reads y through a transposed view reads the update's own output (regression)
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

```python
import torch


def f(x):
    y = x + x.sum(-2, keepdim=True)
    mask = y.roll(-1, -2) == y.transpose(-1, -2)
    y.index_put_((mask,), torch.tensor(7.0))
    return y


x = (torch.arange(100) % 3).float().view(4, 5, 5)
print((f(x) != torch.compile(f)(x)).sum().item())
```

```
7
```

Wrong on CPU and CUDA (7 of 100 elements here, 21 of 147 at 3 x 7 x 7 on CUDA), silently, and with `accumulate=True` too. On 2.14.0 `y[mask] = 7` does the same (the nightly traces that one another way and gets it right); `y.masked_fill_(mask, 7)` is right. 2.14.0 and the nightlies of 21 and 23 Sep are wrong, 2.9.1 is right.

The post-grad graph is fine (`index_put_(add, [eq], full)`, with `eq` reading `add` rolled and permuted). In the generated code the permuted read loads the buffer the fill is writing: the loop body of `buf1` has `ops.load('buf1', 25*p0 + p1 + 5*p2)`, and the C++ kernel does `transpose_mxn(out_ptr1 + ...)` with `out_ptr1 = buf1`, where it should read `buf0` (`add`).

I think this is `mutate_to`'s fast path. `index_put_as_masked_fill` calls `mutate_to(self, where(mask, value, self))`, and since `add` is not an input the fast path swings its StorageBox to the new value (`changed_data.data = val.data`). `add` was already realized (the roll's `index` needs it), so `y.transpose(-1, -2)` was lowered as a ReinterpretView of that StorageBox, and ReinterpretView's loader looks the buffer name up only when it runs, after lowering, when the name is already the fill's. The roll is only there to get `add` realized before the transpose is lowered.

Skipping the fast path when the target is already realized, and writing the value into it with `realize_into` instead, makes these right on CPU and CUDA. I have it with a test and can open a PR.

title: Dynamo runtime overhead in LLM Inference
body: Setup: torch.compile on HF transformers qwen3-8b https://gist.github.com/zou3519/63fa2e77d7fcefe21c73d44e4e9190d6 ## the problem By default it looks like Dynamo cache lookup and pre-graph bytecode take ~2ms. This happens on every forward pass of the model: It's possible that this runtime overhead can matter depending on everything else the user does. The prefill in this profile is 41ms, which is a bit larger than 2ms, but a decode of this is probably going to be closer to 2ms than 41ms. Usually people use cudagraphs (on the outside of torch.compile) and/or make sure their gpu is fully utilized via other strategies, so it's plausible that the Dynamo CPU overhead can be hidden, but 2ms seems like a lot. We should try to bring down the 2ms as much as possible and/or document how to do it if we haven't already. ## some workarounds that bring the times down some noisy codex analysis: ``` Cumulative configuration Cache lookup Pregraph Combined overhead ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ━━━━━━━━━━ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Baseline 0.761 ms 0.131 ms 0.892 ms ─────────────────────────────────────── ────────────── ────────── ─────────────────── + install_free_tensors=True 2.000 ms 0.006 ms 2.006 ms ─────────────────────────────────────── ────────────── ────────── ─────────────────── + skip_guard_eval_unsafe=True 0.105 ms 0.007 ms 0.112 ms ─────────────────────────────────────── ────────────── ────────── ─────────────────── + skip_guard_on_all_nn_modules_unsafe 0.038 ms 0.006 ms 0.044 ms ─────────────────────────────────────── ────────────── ────────── ─────────────────── + skip_all_guards_unsafe 0 ms 0.006 ms 0.006 ms ``` I'm surprised that skip_guard_eval_unsafe=True doesn't just skip all the guards, since I'm just compiling for one specialization. Unrelated but interesting: Inductor freezing mode is highly profitable because it combine the qkv weights all into one big buffer. codex tells me the forward pass latency goes from 20-26ms down to 10ms with freezing on. ## discussion cc @chauhang @penguinwu @voznesenskym @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @kadeng @amjames @jataylo @azahed98 @anijain2305 @williamwen42

title: [RFC] RFC-0036: Zero-GC 64-byte Cache-Aligned Flat Arena for Speculative Decoding Verification
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

This is an RFC tracking issue for a zero-GC, 64-byte cache-line aligned contiguous flat arena allocator tailored for candidate token tree verification in speculative decoding.

* RFC Pull Request: https://github.com/pytorch/rfcs/pull/110
* Discourse Discussion: https://dev-discuss.pytorch.org/t/rfc-0036-zero-gc-64-byte-cache-aligned-flat-arena-for-speculative-decoding-verification/3441

### Problem & Motivation
Speculative decoding verification on autoregressive LLMs generates high-frequency, short-lived token candidate trees. Standard dynamic tensor allocations during candidate branch verification introduce heap churn, memory fragmentation, and GC/synchronization overhead across multi-head verifiers.

### Pitch
By utilizing a flat 64-byte cache-line aligned arena, candidate token trees achieve CPU L1/L2 cache residency, eliminating per-step allocator locks and GC pressure, providing up to 1.83x lower p99 verification latency.


### Alternatives

Standard dynamic allocation via c10 default allocator, or generic out-of-tree pooling extensions that do not guarantee 64-byte L1 cache-line boundary alignment.


### Additional context

We welcome architectural review and feedback from the inference, memory allocator (c10), and performance SIG maintainers regarding integration boundaries.

title: [dynamo] x.contiguous().unsqueeze_(d) / x.to(x.dtype).unsqueeze_(d) crashes guard creation with IndexError: list index out of range (in-place view through a no-op alias of the input)
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`x.contiguous()`, `x.to(x.dtype)` and `x.to(x.device)` return `x` itself when they are no-ops. If that result is then mutated in place with a rank-changing view op (`unsqueeze_`, `squeeze_`), Dynamo does not recognise it as a metadata mutation of the graph input and guard creation crashes with `IndexError: list index out of range` in `produce_guards_verbose`. The same mutation applied directly to the input (`x.unsqueeze_(0)`, fixed in #129673) works.

```python
import torch

def fn(x):
    v = x.contiguous()   # x is contiguous -> v is x
    v.unsqueeze_(2)
    return x

x = torch.arange(24, dtype=torch.int64).reshape(4, 6)
fn(x.clone())                                   # eager: fine, x becomes (4, 6, 1)
torch.compile(fn, backend="eager")(x.clone())   # IndexError: list index out of range
```

|---|---|
| `x.contiguous().unsqueeze_(2)` | IndexError |
| `x.to(x.dtype).unsqueeze_(2)` | IndexError |
| `x.to(x.device).unsqueeze_(2)` | IndexError |
| `v = x.contiguous(); w = v.view(torch.int32); v.unsqueeze_(2); w.clamp_(-3, 4)` | IndexError |
| `x.unsqueeze_(2)`, `x.squeeze_(0)` (direct) | OK |
| `x.requires_grad_(False).unsqueeze_(2)` | OK |
| `x.contiguous().transpose_(0, 1)` (rank-preserving) | OK |
| `x.detach().unsqueeze_(2)`, `x.view_as(x).unsqueeze_(2)` (new objects) | OK |

A related internal assertion from a random program generator, when a rank-preserving mutation goes through the same kind of alias together with other uses: `AssertionError: Guard failed on the same frame it was created. This is a bug - please create an issue. Guard fail reason: 0/0: t0.stride()[1] == t0.size()[0]`.

Identical on torch 2.14.0 and nightly 2.15.0.dev20260921, with `backend="eager"`, `"aot_eager"` and `"inductor"`.

### Root cause

`TensorVariable.var_getattr` only turns in-place view ops into a (delayed) graph break when `self.source is not None`. The generic `call_method` path builds a fresh, source-less `TensorVariable` for the result of `contiguous()`/`to()`, although its example value *is* the input's fake tensor. The subsequent `unsqueeze_` therefore mutates the input's fake tensor behind the recorded guards. A PR that returns the same `VariableTracker` when a non-mutating method's example value is the receiver's example value, plus a regression test in `test/dynamo/test_repros.py`, follows.

title: [XPU] torch.xpu.empty_cache() silently corrupts index_add_ results to all-NaN after a heavy kernel chain (Arc A-Series, Windows)
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Calling `torch.xpu.empty_cache()` right after submitting a reduction (`index_add_`) that is fed by a long asynchronous kernel chain **silently corrupts the reduction result to all-NaN** on Intel Arc A-Series (Alchemist) / Windows. No error, no crash — the program keeps running with wrong data. The corruption is deterministic in the setup below (7/7 runs in separate processes).

This is the "silent wrong results" sibling of the `AssertHandler::printMessage` crash in #157714 (same workload, same hardware class; the crash itself is currently intermittent on this machine, the data corruption is not).

**Environment:** Windows 11, Intel Arc A730M, driver 32.0.101.8992, torch 2.14.0+xpu (Python 3.14).

**Reproducer (self-contained):**

```python
import torch

def _v2(x):
    lowbit = x & -x
    v = torch.round(lowbit.to(torch.float32).log2())
    return torch.where(x > 0, v, torch.zeros_like(v)).to(torch.int64)

def kronecker_chain(Dv, nf, rounds=160):
    a = torch.as_tensor(Dv, dtype=torch.int64, device=nf.device)
    if a.dim() == 0:
        a = a.expand(nf.shape)
    nabs = nf.abs()
    v2 = _v2(nabs)
    n_odd = torch.where(nabs > 0, nabs >> v2, nabs)
    res = torch.ones_like(n_odd)
    res = torch.where((v2 > 0) & (a % 2 == 0), torch.zeros_like(res), res)
    a8 = a % 8
    base8 = torch.where((a8 == 1) | (a8 == 7), torch.ones_like(res), -torch.ones_like(res))
    res = torch.where((v2 % 2 == 1) & (a % 2 == 1), base8.expand_as(res), res)
    m = torch.where(n_odd > 0, n_odd, torch.ones_like(n_odd))
    a_j = torch.where(n_odd > 0, a % m, torch.zeros_like(m))
    jr = torch.ones_like(m)
    for _ in range(rounds):
        active = a_j != 0
        tz = _v2(a_j)
        shifted = a_j >> tz
        m8 = m % 8
        flip = ((m8 == 3) | (m8 == 5)) & (tz % 2 == 1)
        a_j = torch.where(active, shifted, a_j)
        jr = torch.where(active & flip, -jr, jr)
        a_old, m_old = a_j, m
        a_j = torch.where(active, m_old, a_old)
        m = torch.where(active, a_old, m_old)
        flip2 = (a_j % 4 == 3) & (m % 4 == 3)
        jr = torch.where(active & flip2, -jr, jr)
        m_safe = torch.where(m != 0, m, torch.ones_like(m))
        a_j = torch.where(active, a_j % m_safe, a_j)
    jacobi_out = torch.where(m == 1, jr, torch.zeros_like(jr))
    res = res * jacobi_out
    out = torch.where(nf == 0, torch.where(a.abs() == 1, torch.ones_like(res), torch.zeros_like(res)), res)
    mult = torch.where(a < 0, -torch.ones_like(out), torch.ones_like(out))
    return torch.where(nf < 0, out * mult, out)

def heavy_block(dvals):
    counts = torch.tensor([D - 1 for D in dvals], dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu')
    seg = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(len(dvals), dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu'), counts)
    n_rel = torch.arange(seg.numel(), dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu') - (torch.cumsum(counts, 0) - counts)[seg]
    start_n = torch.ones(len(dvals), dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu'); start_n[0] = 1
    nf = n_rel + start_n[seg]
    Dval = torch.tensor(dvals, dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu')[seg]
    chi = kronecker_chain(Dval, nf).float()
    logv = torch.log(torch.clamp(torch.abs(
        2.0 * torch.sin(torch.pi * nf.to(torch.float32) / Dval.to(torch.float32))),
        min=torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny))
    return seg, chi * logv

def fundamental_discriminants(limit):
    out = []
    for D in range(2, limit + 1):
        if D % 4 == 1 and _squarefree(D):
            out.append(D)
        elif D % 4 == 0:
            m = D // 4
            if m % 4 in (2, 3) and _squarefree(m):
                out.append(D)
    return out

def _squarefree(n):
    d = 2
    while d * d <= n:
        if n % (d * d) == 0:
            return False
        d += 1
    return True

dvals = fundamental_discriminants(11000)          # 3342 discriminants, T ~10.3M elements
seg, prod = heavy_block(dvals)
S = torch.zeros(len(dvals), dtype=torch.float32, device='xpu')
S.index_add_(0, seg, prod)
torch.xpu.empty_cache()                            # <-- trigger
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print(S[0].item())                                 # nan (expected -0.962424...)
```

Output: `S[0] = nan`, and all 3342 entries of `S` are non-finite (`(~torch.isfinite(S)).sum() == 3342`).

### Expected behavior

`S[0] == -0.962424...` (the correct value; `empty_cache()` must not change already-computed results).

### Control experiments (same chain, same data)

| variant | result |
|---|---|
| no `empty_cache()` | correct (`-0.962424...`) |
| `S[0].item()` read before `empty_cache()` | correct — the D2H copy appears to drain the driver's deferred state |
| `torch.xpu.synchronize()` before `empty_cache()` | still corrupted (at least once; intermittent) |
| plain `index_add_` without the chain (10M/50M elements) + `empty_cache()` | correct |
| chain tensors dropped (function scope) before `empty_cache()` | correct — tensors must stay referenced |

The corruption depends on `empty_cache()` hitting the driver's deferred state left by the heavy chain, with the reduction's inputs still referenced. It is deterministic in the exact script above (7/7 separate processes), but sensitive to process history — likely the same family as the CUDA-side `empty_cache()`-frees-memory-with-queued-writers bugs #196257 / #196258, and it means any long-running XPU workload that calls `empty_cache()` risks silent data corruption.

Also on this hardware: the same chain with a *second* write to the same tensor crashes with `AssertHandler::printMessage` + SIGSEGV (see #157714; currently intermittent).

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.14.0+xpu
OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
Python version: 3.14
Intel GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) A730M Graphics (Alchemist, device_id 0x5691)
Driver: 32.0.101.8992
```

title: [Windows][AOTInductor] `aoti_compile_and_package()` hangs in `torch._inductor.codecache.format_consts_to_cpp()` when compiling an nnUNetv2 model
body:
## Bug description

AOTInductor compilation of an nnUNetv2 model hangs indefinitely on Windows after successful export. The same model compiles successfully in a Linux environment.

`torch.export.export()` completes successfully and the exported model passes correctness validation. However, `torch._inductor.aoti_compile_and_package()` never returns.

Using `py-spy` after more than 30 minutes of runtime consistently shows the main thread inside `torch._inductor.codecache.format_consts_to_cpp()`.


---

## Reproduction script

```python
import json, torch
from nnunetv2.utilities.plans_handling.plans_handler import PlansManager
from nnunetv2.utilities.get_network_from_plans import get_network_from_plans

MODEL_DIR = r"Path\to\SPACEtomo_lamella_segmentation_Yeast\model"
CONFIG = "2d"

plans = json.load(open(f"{MODEL_DIR}\\plans.json"))
dataset_json = json.load(open(f"{MODEL_DIR}\\dataset.json"))
pm = PlansManager(plans)
cfg = pm.get_configuration(CONFIG)

ckpt = torch.load(
```

title: [inductor] fp32 SDPA fusion: _sfdp_pattern_24 skips _sfdp_params_check, and the gate it skips is wrong on ROCm
body:
Two coupled defects in the fp32 SDPA fusion gate in `torch/_inductor/fx_passes/fuse_attention.py`. Filing as one issue because fixing the first without the second regresses ROCm.

**1. `_sfdp_pattern_24` never runs its extra check.**

At line 1338 the pattern is registered with the factory passed uncalled:

```python
(
    _sfdp_pattern_24,
    _sfdp_replacement_24,
    [g(), g(), g(), b_float()],
    {},
    _sfdp_extra_check,        # every other site passes _sfdp_extra_check(...) or _sfdp_params_check
),
```

`_sfdp_extra_check(scale_factor_op=None, disable_cuda=False)` is a factory returning an inner `fn`. The matcher calls `extra_check(match)` at `pattern_matcher.py:2141`, which binds `scale_factor_op=match` and returns that inner closure -- a truthy function object. So the check always "passes" and `_sfdp_params_check` never runs for this pattern.

That means pattern 24 skips all four of its validations: the `inv_scale` check, the q/k/v dtype-and-device consistency check, the tf32 gate, and the attn_mask dtype/device/rank check. The pattern takes a mask (`b_float()`), so the mask validation is not vacuous.

**2. The tf32 gate's premise is inverted on ROCm.**

```python
# fused kernels use tf32
if (query.device.type == "cuda" and query.dtype == torch.float32
        and torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision != "tf32"):
    return False
```

On ROCm the fused kernel does not use reduced precision. `_fused_sdp_choice` selects AOTriton mem-efficient attention, which computes in full fp32 and is bit-identical whether the flag says `ieee` or `tf32`. Measured on gfx942 against an fp64 gold at shapes (4,2,16,32) with a mask: the fused result is 2.456e-06 from gold under both settings, while the eager `bmm` reference degrades from 2.41e-06 to 6.04e-03 because hipBLASLt honors the flag as XF32. Same picture on gfx950 (7.44e-05). So on ROCm the gate refuses to fuse in exactly the configuration where the fused kernel is the more accurate one.

**Why they are one issue.**

Fixing (1) alone regresses ROCm. Changing line 1338 to `_sfdp_extra_check()` makes `test_pattern_fails_with_mismatched_view_grouping_gpu` fail immediately with `AssertionError: 0 not greater than or equal to 1` on the `fuse_attention` counter, because that test now runs at `ieee` on ROCm (#198220 follow-up) and the gate then refuses the fusion. Fixing (2) alone is safe but leaves pattern 24 unchecked.

Repro for (1), on any device:

```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
from torch._dynamo.utils import counters
bs, n_head, seq_len, embed_dim = 4, 2, 16, 32

def f(q, k, v, mask):
    qq = q.view(bs*n_head, seq_len, embed_dim)
    kk = k.reshape(bs*n_head, seq_len, embed_dim)
    vv = v.reshape(bs*n_head, seq_len, embed_dim)
    w = torch.bmm(qq, kk.transpose(1, 2))
    w = (w.view(bs, n_head, seq_len, seq_len) + mask).view(bs*n_head, seq_len, seq_len)
    return torch.bmm(F.softmax(w, dim=-1), vv).view(bs, n_head, seq_len, embed_dim)

for prec in ("tf32", "ieee"):
    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = prec
    torch._dynamo.reset(); counters.clear()
    args = [torch.randn(bs, n_head, seq_len, embed_dim, device="cuda") for _ in range(3)]
    args.append(torch.randn(1, 1, seq_len, seq_len, device="cuda"))
    torch.compile(f, fullgraph=True)(*args)
    print(prec, counters["inductor"]["fuse_attention"])
```

Both print `1`. With the gate actually wired up, `ieee` should print `0` on CUDA.

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

This is found by our fuzzer, here is the code to reproduce:

```

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

    def forward(self, x):
        b = x.expand(2, *x.shape)
        b[0, 0] = 1.0
        idx = (b[0].to(torch.int64))

torch.manual_seed(0)
x1 = torch.tensor([[ -1.5410, -0.2934],
        [-2.1788,  0.5684]])
torch.manual_seed(0)

        [-2.1788,  0.5684]])

out1 = model(x1)
print(out1)
'''
tensor([[ 1,  1],
        [-2,  0]])
'''
out2 = cmodel(x2)
'''
tensor([[ 0,  1],
        [-2,  0]])
'''

torch.testing.assert_close(out1, out2)
```

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!

Mismatched elements: 1 / 4 (25.0%)
```

2. The in-place assignment b[0, 0] = 1.0 is executed first.
3. The slice b[0] (the entire first row) is converted to int64 via .to(torch.int64). Converting b[0, 0] instead does not trigger the bug.

title: flex_attention returns incorrect output under Inductor when seq_len < block size
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`flex_attention` returns incorrect output under Inductor when `seq_len` is below the 128 mask block size and a pointwise op feeds q/k.

Tested the following masks. The values below show the difference from the corresponding implementation with SDPA.

| `mask_mod` @ seq_len 32, Inductor | vs same-mask SDPA | 
|---|---|
| **no-op (`lambda b,h,q,kv: kv >= 0`)** | **3.518e-01** |
| causal | 8.979e-01 |
| anti-causal (`kv >= q`) | 8.080e-01 |
| sliding-window causal | 8.979e-01 | 
| block-diagonal | 5.997e-01 | 

Interestingly, even with the trivial mask, we still see a difference, so it's not a matter of the mask being ignored. On all of these tests, we found that `flex_attention` matches sdpa when using eager and `aot_eager`, and we only see this discrepancy when using Inductor.

This issue was authored with the assistance of an AI coding assistant; the analysis and reproductions were reviewed and verified by the submitter.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
"""flex_attention returns incorrect output under Inductor when seq_len < 128.

A plain causal BlockMask is compared against F.scaled_dot_product_attention
with is_causal=True. They must agree. Under Inductor they do not, when
seq_len is below the 128 mask block size AND a pointwise op feeds q/k --
with q/k passed straight from the projection, every length is exact.

The `pointwise` column is the control: same shapes, same mask, only the
producer of q/k differs.

Pass/fail is torch.testing.assert_close at its default tolerances (fp32:
rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5); the printed column is the max absolute difference,
for information only. RNG equivalence is structural rather than configured --
`got` and `want` are computed from the same weights and the same input, and
the model contains no random ops.

    python flex_bug.py     # exits non-zero if any configuration mismatches
"""

import sys

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.nn.attention.flex_attention import create_block_mask, flex_attention

DEV = torch.device("cuda")
B, H, D = 2, 4, 32
DIM = H * D


class CausalAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, pointwise: bool):
        super().__init__()
        self.pointwise = pointwise
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(DIM, 3 * DIM, bias=False)
        self.register_buffer("scale", torch.rand(D) + 0.5)

    def qkv_of(self, x):
        b, s, _ = x.shape
        q, k, v = self.qkv(x).view(b, s, 3, H, D).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        if self.pointwise:
            q, k = q * self.scale, k * self.scale
        return q, k, v

    def forward(self, x, block_mask):
        q, k, v = self.qkv_of(x)
        return flex_attention(q, k, v, block_mask=block_mask, scale=D**-0.5)


def causal_block_mask(seq_len):
    def mask_mod(b, h, q_idx, kv_idx):
        return kv_idx <= q_idx

    return create_block_mask(mask_mod, B=None, H=None, Q_LEN=seq_len, KV_LEN=seq_len, device=DEV)


def check(seq_len, pointwise, backend):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    model = CausalAttention(pointwise).to(DEV).eval()
    gen = torch.Generator(device=DEV).manual_seed(0)
    x = torch.randn(B, seq_len, DIM, device=DEV, generator=gen)

    torch._dynamo.reset()
    run = model if backend == "eager" else torch.compile(model, backend=backend)
    with torch.no_grad():
        got = run(x, causal_block_mask(seq_len))
        q, k, v = model.qkv_of(x)
        want = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True, scale=D**-0.5)

    err = (got - want).abs().max().item()
    try:
        torch.testing.assert_close(got, want)
        mismatch = False
    except AssertionError:
        mismatch = True

    del model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return err, mismatch


print(f"torch {torch.__version__}   {torch.cuda.get_device_name()}")
print(f"\n{'seq_len':>8} {'pointwise q/k':>14} {'backend':>11} "
      f"{'vs is_causal SDPA':>18}")
failures = 0
for seq_len in (32, 64, 128, 256):
    for pointwise in (True, False):
        for backend in ("eager", "aot_eager", "inductor"):
            err, bad = check(seq_len, pointwise, backend)
            failures += bad
            print(f"{seq_len:>8} {str(pointwise):>14} {backend:>11} "
                  f"{err:>18.3e}   {'MISMATCH' if bad else 'ok'}")

print(f"\n{failures} mismatching configuration(s)")
sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```

### Ablation (H200, torch 2.11.0+cu128)

Ablating `backend` (eager / aot_eager / inductor) against the presence of the pointwise op on q/k, across `seq_len`. Only inductor + pointwise + `seq_len < 128` fails.

```
      32           True    inductor          8.979e-01   MISMATCH
      32          False       eager          4.172e-07   ok

     128           True       eager          3.576e-07   ok

     128          False       eager          3.576e-07   ok

     256          False   aot_eager          3.576e-07   ok
     256          False    inductor          3.576e-07   ok

2 mismatching configuration(s)
```

### AI-generated analysis

The original experiments we were running were in the context of transformers using RoPE embeddings, but upon finding this bug, we explored a bit further to find out if there were specific conditions needed to cause them. The list below is an AI summary that describes the situations in which we saw the incorrect output.

```
- **Inductor codegen.** `eager` and `aot_eager` are exact on the identical model, so tracing, functionalization and AOTAutograd are not involved.
- **Requires a fused pointwise producer on q/k.** The `pointwise` column is an in-table control: same shapes, same mask, only the q/k producer differs. One broadcast multiply is enough. (We first hit this via RoPE; RoPE is incidental, and its `cat` is not required.)
- **Strictly below the block size, not "not a multiple of" it.** Leaks at 32/64/96/120/127; exact at 128/129/130/160/200/256/300/384/512/1000/2048. 160 and 200 carry a partial trailing block and are fine.
- **Not GPU-specific.** Identical boundary and drift on A100 (108 SMs), H100 (132) and H200, in fp32 and bf16 alike.
- **Not fixed by upgrading.** Bit-identical drift on torch 2.11.0+cu128, 2.13.0+cu129 and 2.14.0+cu130 — deterministic codegen behaviour rather than a race.
- **Specific to FlexAttention.** The same masking expressed as a dense boolean mask through `scaled_dot_product_attention` is exact at every length, eager and compiled.

One suggestive detail: an earlier probe of ours appeared clean because the compiled function *returned* q/k alongside the output, forcing them to be materialized. That is consistent with a prologue-fusion fault.
```

[torch_trace.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32618434/torch_trace.tar.gz)

### Not a duplicate of

- **#159247** (flex decoding / paged attention, `Q_S=1`, "KV length not a multiple of block size") — non-multiples above 128 are exact here, so "not a multiple" is not the condition; this is full attention in fp32.
- **#163588** (bfloat16 numerical instability with masks, closed as iterative-softmax precision) — this reproduces in fp32

None. `torch.compile` reports success and returns a tensor of the expected dtype and shape whose values are wrong.
